tables: STANDARD 23: PROVISION OF AND CONTINUITY OF CARE (MANDATORY STANDARD)

STANDARD: The Healthcare Organisation ensures patients are provided with safe, high- quality inpatient and outpatient care throughout the care delivery process. They should do this from the time that the patient enters the healthcare organisation or service through to when the patient is discharged or transferred to another health facility-service; and during any ongoing care they provide after discharge.
The Healthcare Organisation should implement evidence-based practice and a have a process for assessing the appropriateness and effectiveness of care and services, and the settings they are delivered in.
Source(s)
Standard 17 National Health Service Standards (NHSS) Vol. 2 (2nd Edition) National Quality Standard

ORGANISATION AND MANAGEMENT

Pathology Services may be provided by a laboratory or laboratories within, or external to the Facility. The Pathology Services may include anatomical pathology, chemical pathology, haematology, microbiology and genetics. The services shall be organised and administered to provide a comprehensive and quality diagnostic service which is innovative, efficient and reliable for quality and safe patient care.

The Vision, Mission of the Facility are visible. The Goals of the Oncology Services suit its scope and are clearly documented. It should reflect the aspirations of the service and the needs of the community.
All off-site hospital laboratory under the purview of Pathology Services shall be included in the main organisation chart.
Evidence of Compliance
The Mission, Vision and Goals of the Organisation are visible, endorsed and dated.
There is an endorsed and dated department organisational chart with lines of functions and reporting relationships (including with off-site hospital facilities being serviced).
Relevant policies and guidelines are available in the department, i.e., National Health Plan, National Health Service Standards, etc.).
Evidence of submission of an Annual Implementation Plan and budget.
Evidence of fee structure (if fees are collected).

There is a mechanism to ensure effective interaction between the Head of the Services and the Organisation’s Governing Body and Senior Management. The Head of Services shall also be involved for the following aspects of management of the services;
Preparation of budget and ensuring that expenditure remains within the budget allocated
Human resource 
Facility and equipment management
Safety and performance improvement activities and risk management
Evidence of Compliance
Letter of appointment and terms of reference as the Head of Service
Letter of appointment and terms of reference in other hospital committees.
Evidence of (a) to (d) in meeting minutes/corespondence of the Pathology Services indicating the involvement of the Head of Service.
Request for allocation for budget and staffing.

Regular staff meetings are held between Head of Service and staff with sufficient regularity to discuss issues pertaining to the Pathology Services. These meetings are minuted and communicated to all staff.
Evidence of Compliance
Meeting minutes are available, disseminated and acknowledged by staff.
There is sufficient attendance for the meetings with adequate representatives of the service.
Frequency of meetings are as scheduled.
Discussions and resolutions are implemented. (problems not solved are brought forward to the next meeting till resolved).

Appropriate statistics and records are maintained in the department in and used for managing services and patient care. The following (among others) are available;
Workload/census for inpatients and outpatients
Quarterly and annual report
Incident reports and register
Staffing number and staff profile
Staff training records
Data on performance improvement
Number of referrals
Number of autopsies performed (hospital/coroner’s case)
Evidence of Compliance
The statistics and records  from (a) to (h) are available.
The NHSS Toolkit Assessment (checklist) for the relevant level has been completed in the past 6 months.
Facilities that do not have their own Pathology Services or cannot provide a full range of laboratory services, can arrange with an external laboratory or laboratories to provide the services needed.
Evidence of Compliance
There is a written agreement with the external laboratory.
The type and nature of tests and investigation that are available is specified.
Requests for tests/investigations should be documented in a register.
There is a safe mode of transport of specimens.
There is provision for immediate communication of results which are “out of the normal” range.
There are arrangements for after-hours and emergency work.
There are quality systems in place  e.g. the lab participants in External Quality Assurance (EQA) activities.
HUMAN RESOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT

The Pathology Services shall be directed by a qualified and competent medical practitioner, and staffed by suitably qualified and competent staff to achieve the goals and objectives of the Pathology Services. There are sufficient staffing levels, a staff supervision structure, performance appraisals and ongoing commitment to continuing medical education.

The are written and dated job descriptions for each category of staff that include;
Qualification, training and experience for the position
Lines of authority
Accountability, functions and responsibilities
Reviewed when required if there is major change in job scope 
Statutory regulations
Administrative and clinical job scope
Evidence of Compliance
There are dated and specific job descriptions for each staff that include (a) to (f).
The job description is acknowledged by the staff and signed by the Head of Service and dated.
The scope of work in the job description aligns with the training, skill and experience of the staff (credentialling).
The staff holds current registration with the relevant professional body.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of current registration for all cadres of staff (annual practicing certificate).
The staff works within their job description and job scope.
Evidence of Compliance
Observation that cadres of staff are working according to their job description and job scope.
There are continuing education activities for staff to pursue professional interests and to prepare for current and future changes in practice.
Evidence of Compliance
Training calendar includes in-house/ external courses/ workshops/ conferences.
Training for each staff including training in life support is kept in the Department.
There are ongoing Continuous Professional Activities in the Department.
The educational needs of staff are addressed following findings from incidents reports, mortality audits and performance improvement studies.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of staff training because of recommendations made from incident reports or mortality and morbidity reviews.
Where applicable, the functions of the Pathology Services include undergraduate, postgraduate and other health professional education, research projects and special studies, as appropriate.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of sufficient skilled trained staff to provide supervision as per terms of Memorandum of Understanding.
There is a Memorandum of Understanding with the relevant institution/entity.
Staff including medical practitioners receive evaluation of their performance at the completion of the probationary period and annually thereafter, or as defined by the Organisation.
Evidence of Compliance
Performance appraisal for staff including medical practitioners is completed upon probationary period and as an annual exercise.
Where appropriate, the Facility shall endeavour to undertake clinical research using available resources.
Evidence of Compliance
Documented evidence of research activities in the Department.
The Pathology Services shall provide a continuing education activity for non-laboratory health professional staff to keep them informed of matters related to Pathology Services.
Evidence of Compliance
Continuing medical education for non-laboratory health professional staff.
Records on attendance.

There is a structured orientation programme for all newly appointed staff to the Pathology Services including medical practitioners and for those new to specific areas that include the following;
Explanation of the goals, objectives, policies and procedures of the Facility and those of the Pathology Services
Lines of authority and areas of responsibility 
Explanation of duties and functions
Rules and regulations especially related to health hazards and safety precautions
Handover communication
Staff appraisal procedures for the Pathology Services
Requirements for immunisation against certain high-risk diseases
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of policy stating that all staff have to attend a structured orientation programme.
Attendance list of those having attended the orientation programme.
POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

There are written and dated policies for all activities of the Pathology Services which reflect current knowledge and principles of laboratory practice.
They are consistent with statutory requirements and the objectives of the Pathology Services. There are current Laboratory User Manual and documented Standard Operating Procedures Manual available for staff reference.

There are written policies and procedures for the Pathology Services which are consistent with the overall policies of the Facility, regulatory requirements and current standard practices. These policies include;
The conduct of professional activities in accordance with the ethical standards of the professions involved
Provide ready but controlled access to laboratory results 
Introduction of new tests, improvement on techniques, and undertaking research, where appropriate
Provision of services on a 24-hour basis 
Contribution to the provision of high- quality patient care by assisting in the review and evaluation of clinical practice within the Facility 
Provision of consultative service for the medical profession and other relevant staff in the selection of the laboratory investigations, their interpretation, and repeat test if required 
Communication with medical, nursing, and other relevant staff on matters related to the services provided. 
Internal and external disaster plan 
Identify, assess and manage risks.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of documented policies and procedures  (a) to (i) for the service.
The policies and procedures are endorsed and dated.
There is a periodic review at least once in three years.
Copies of policies, by laws, regulations and relevant acts are accessible on site for staff reference.
Policies and procedures are developed by a committee in collaboration with staff and with other departments if needed.
Evidence of Compliance
Minutes of committee meetings on development and revision on policies and procedures.
Staff are aware of these policies and procedures.
Evidence of Compliance
Training or briefing on the policies (meeting minutes or circulation acknowledgement).
There is evidence of compliance with the policies and procedures.
Evidence of Compliance
Verify observation on practices on-site.
Interview staff on procedures.
Review audits on practices (if there are any).

There are policies and procedures relating to requests for laboratory tests which include;
Authorised person who can request for the test
Written confirmation of all verbal request 
Identification of the patient by full name, medical record number, date of birth and sex 
Relevant medical history of patient
Relevant medications of patient
Tests requested
Name of the requesting doctor
Identification of the nature of the specimen on the request form and clear labelling of specimens requiring precautionary handling
Evidence of Compliance
Documented policies and procedures relating to laboratory tests including (a) to (h).

There are written instructions for the proper collection, labelling, storage, preservation and transportation of specimens; and safety measures to be observed.
These instructions are readily accessible to all staff who may be involved in obtaining specimens from patients.
There are written policies determining the length of time for which reports and specimens are retained.
Evidence of Compliance
There is laboratory user guide available.
There is proof that the user guide has been sighted by laboratory services staff.
Observe and verify practice during survey.
Policy is available on how long reports and specimens should be retained.

All pathology reports of investigations done on-site or off-site are included in the patient's medical record: 
Copies of all pathology reports are promptly sent to be reviewed and filed in the patient's medical record. 
Report/forms/results are designed to facilitate comparison of sequential tests/reports. 
There is provision for immediate communication of results with critical range. 
When the reports are communicated via phone, the results are documented in the patient’s notes with the following details;
the person providing the report
the person receiving the report
patient identity
pathology results
date and time of receipt of the results
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of reports in patient’s records (observed).
Evidence that critical results were informed (documentation).
Evidence of documentation of reports received by phone in the patient’s medical records.
Frozen section reports are transmitted directly to the surgeon concerned and followed by a written report.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of communication with the respective surgeon.
Copy of result is observed in the patient’s record.
There is evidence that there are Standards Precaution and Safety guidelines available specifically for Pathology Services.
Evidence of Compliance
Documented safety procedures specific to the Pathology Services.
Record of training/briefing of staff on these safety guidelines.
FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT
Adequate facilities and equipment are available for the safe and efficient provision of Pathology Services taking into consideration the potentially hazardous circumstances of the operations.
The office is separated from the technical laboratory area.
Evidence of Compliance
On-site observation that the office space complies with the above.
Layout of the laboratory complies with the set requirements.
There are designated areas for handling of potentially hazardous material.
Evidence of Compliance

Designated areas include;
Reception to receive samples
Separation
Storage area
Dispatch area
Work benches shall be adequately spaced and arranged in such a way as to ensure safety and efficiency in the use of equipment in accordance with manufacturer's recommendation and safety regulations.
Evidence of Compliance
There are adequate and proper storage areas of reagents, tissue specimens, consumables and other materials
Evidence of Compliance
There are separate and suitable stores for inflammable solvents and acid.
Evidence of Compliance
Onsite observation on separate storage for inflammables and acids according to guidelines.
There are suitably located staff facilities for emergency shower and eye wash, changing room, locker facilities and storage for protective clothing.
Evidence of Compliance

Observation onsite on the availability of;
Emergency shower
Eye wash
Locker facilities
Storage for protective clothing
There is suitable, adequate and safe provision for air conditioning, ventilation, lighting, power, gases, water and drainage in the laboratory.
Evidence of Compliance
On-site observation of adequate ventilation with fume extraction.
Adequate power supply and suitable location of power sockets.
Adequate lighting.
Supply of gases follow safety regulations.
Adequate supply of de-ionised and distilled water for laboratory use
The pathology equipment is appropriate and adequate to meet the demands of the service and are properly maintained.
Evidence of Compliance
On-site observation of adequate equipment suitable to the service.
There is proper equipment maintenance (see maintenance record)
Availability of a back-up system
There is a dedicated cabinet for dangerous drugs which can be locked.
Where specialised equipment is used, there is evidence that only staff who are trained and authorised by the Facility operate such equipment.
Evidence of Compliance
User training records.
List of staff trained and authorised to operate specialised equipment.
Inventory of equipment, reagents and consumables shall be maintained.
Evidence of Compliance
On site observation of record ot equipment inventory.
On site observation of record of reagent inventory.
Onsite observation of record of consumable inventory
Each equipment/instrument has a logbook and maintenance record and these shall be made available when required.
Evidence of Compliance
Observe the equipment/instrument log book.
Equipment/instrument maintenance record.

There is evidence that the facility has a comprehensive maintenance programme such as predictive maintenance, planned preventive maintenance and calibration activities, to ensure the facilities and equipment are in good working order.
Evidence of Compliance
There is observed preventive maintenance schedule.
There is an asset inventory.
There is a complaint records on equipment made.
There is evidence of general cleanliness in the laboratory. There are proper facilities for the disposal of biohazard material as either effluent or containerised material.
Evidence of Compliance
There is a cleaning schedule.
Good housekeeping is evidenced.
There is proper disposal of biohazardous material.
SAFETY AND PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT ACTIVITIES
The Head of Pathology Services shall ensure the provision of quality performance with staff involvement in the continuous safety and performance improvement activities of the Pathology Services.
There are planned activities for performance and quality improvement.
Evidence of Compliance
There is a designated person who monitors safety and performance improvement activities within the Dental Services.
There are records/registers on performance improvement activities.
There are meeting minutes for performance improvement meetings.
There are records on innovation (if any).

The Head of Pathology Services shall ensure that the staff are trained and complete incident reports which are promptly reported, investigated, discussed by the staff and forwarded to the Officer in Charge (OIC) of the Facility. Selected incidents have Root Cause Analysis (RCA) done in an agreed time frame to prevent recurrence.
Evidence of Compliance

System for incident reporting is in place with the following;
Training of staff in incident reporting
Policy on incident reporting
Method/SOP on Incident reporting
Register of incidents
Completed incident reports.
Corrective and preventive action plans.
Minutes of meeting.
Involved staff given feedback about the incident report.
Acknowledgment by Head of Pathology Service and Director of Curative Services.
Evidence of Compliance
Specific performance indicators are monitored.
Remedial action is taken when appropriate.
The Pathology Services has quality control programmes for all tests provided.
Evidence of Compliance
There is an Internal Quality Control (ICQ) Programme
There is an External Quality Control (ECQ) Programme
